messages:
alex: Hey team — question about parental leave timing + paperwork. Partner due 2025-02-10. I'm planning ~12 weeks off. Quick Qs: 1) When should I start the paperwork with People Ops? 2) Can I split the leave (6w + 6w) within the first 6 months? 3) How does short-term disability (STD) / paytop-up work here, and what happens to benefits while I'm out? Also need a checklist for handover/coverage for my ICs. cc @jen (People Ops)
jen (People Ops): Congrats, Alex!! 🎉 Short answers upfront: start paperwork ~30 days prior if you can, splitting is allowed but requires manager + People Ops sign-off, and STD/Redwood top-up interacts depending on eligibility. I'll drop a checklist and the leave-request link in a sec. See internal guide: https://redwoodinference.hq/leave-policy (internal)
sam (Payroll): FYI from payroll side: Redwood provides an 8-week base top-up for eligible full-time employees; beyond that, unpaid unless you have STD approved. Important: submit STD claim as soon as leave starts (or just before) to avoid delays. Payroll needs approved leave docs within 30 days of start to process retro pay/top-up. If you want the company top-up spread across payroll we can arrange — ping me.
lisa (Benefits): Health coverage: employer portion continues for up to 12 weeks of approved parental leave. If leave extends beyond 12 weeks unpaid, we'll invoice you for the employee share or you can elect COBRA depending on the duration. I'll DM the exact premium numbers and the benefits continuity form.
maria (Manager): From a coverage POV I can: 1) assign Emily to be interim owner of Priorsync, 2) freeze noncritical roadmaps, 3) set up weekly async status doc. Alex — can you sketch the 2-week handoff plan? I'll block overlap time for knowledge transfer.
jen (People Ops): Ok checklist (quick):
```
- Submit internal leave request: https://redwoodinference.hq/leave-request
- Upload partner/placement docs (DOB or adoption paperwork)
- If applying for STD: file claim with VendorX and attach physician/placement docs
- Manager signs coverage plan + return-to-work schedule
- People Ops approves & confirms benefits continuation dates
- Schedule a payroll sync (sam) before first payroll cutoff after leave starts
- Create a handover doc and share with team + backup
```
Notes: ideally start steps 30 days out. Splitting: you can request up to 2 blocks within 12 months, but we need the manager to confirm coverage and People Ops to approve dates to ensure benefits/top-up calculations.
hr-bot: Reminder created: 'Parental leave paperwork deadline' (3 weeks before 2025-02-10) — scheduled on your calendar, alex.
emily: I can take the day-to-day incident paging and own sprint tickets while you're out. If you want, add a short runbook section: 'how to triage Priorsync alerts' — I can draft it.
sam (Payroll): Alex, small payroll detail: if your leave spans a payroll cutoff, we need the approved leave start date by the pay period close (typically 7 days before payout). If paperwork is late we can still do retro payments but it'll be on the next cycle after approval.
jen (People Ops): Templates attached in DM; sample return-to-work options: full-time on X date, phased (80% -> 60% -> full) over 4 weeks, or part-time with manager approval. If you plan a phased return, include desired hours/days in the leave request.
alex: Awesome — super helpful. I'll fill out the internal form today and upload docs. Maria, I'll draft a 2-week handover + runbook and tag Emily. Thanks everyone! :heart:
__notes: Document follows agents.md: Slack thread with messages in chronological order. No title field included.
